learn.title: How cases work
learn.intro: In German, the article changes depending on the noun's role in the sentence. This role is called the case. Ask the question word to find it, then look up the article in the table.
steps: Find the gender of the noun: der, die, das or plural.
Find the case: is there a verb or preposition that decides it? If not, is the noun the subject or the object?
Look up the article where the case row meets the gender column.

nom.use: The subject: the person or thing doing the action. Also after "sein" (to be).
nom.tip: This is the form you learn in the dictionary.

akk.use: The direct object: the person or thing that receives the action.
triggers: Verbs: haben, sehen, kaufen, brauchen, suchen, lieben, fragen, besuchen
Prepositions: durch, für, gegen, ohne, um
Two-way prepositions (in, an, auf…) when there is movement: wohin?
akk.tip: Only masculine changes: der → den, ein → einen.

dat.use: The indirect object: who gets or receives something. Also after some verbs and prepositions.
triggers: Verbs: helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, antworten
Prepositions: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu
Two-way prepositions (in, an, auf, neben, vor, unter…) for a location: wo?
dat.tip: Plural nouns get -n: den Kindern (unless they already end in -n or -s).

gen.use: Possession: whose something is. Also after some prepositions.
gen.tip: Masculine and neuter nouns get -s or -es: des Mannes, des Kindes.
